beats.text: At a barangay health discussion, BHW Riza does more than read a poster. She first learns what residents are asking, then explains clearly.
As a Health Educator, she may discuss care for the body, clean surroundings, and how to reach health services. She uses materials approved by the health team.
An infant's caregiver, a young person, a pregnant resident, and an older adult may have different questions. Riza adapts discussions of illness, accidents, and risks to each life stage.
Riza notices that only parents attended. She asks who else is missing and what time, place, language, and format could help them take part.
To include young people, Riza asks when they can join and what they want to learn. She adapts the discussion to their questions while keeping the information accurate and approved.
BHW health education is a purposeful conversation: listen, choose a suitable topic and approved materials, adapt to life stage, and make participation possible for every group.
